name: Hezekiah and the ambassadors of Babylon
charge: Showing all his treasures to Babylon in the pride of his heart
summary: Healed of a mortal sickness and given fifteen years, Hezekiah received envoys from Babylon and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the armor, everything. Isaiah asked what they had seen. Nothing hidden, said the king.
offense: After receiving healing and a sign, Hezekiah did not render according to the benefit done to him, because his heart was lifted up (2 Chronicles 32:24-25). Mercy received became an occasion for self-regard instead of gratitude. The Babylonian envoys came with letters and a present, and he showed them his treasures, armour, and all that was in his dominion (2 Kings 20:12-15). Chronicles says that God left him to try him and disclose what was in his heart (2 Chronicles 32:31). The trial came through honour and interest, not only through an enemy's threat. The king who had sought the Lord under siege also had to remember him amid admiration.
judgment: Isaiah declared that the treasures would be carried to Babylon and that descendants of the king would serve in its palace (2 Kings 20:16-18). What he displayed as the strength of his house was named as another kingdom's future spoil. Hezekiah and Jerusalem humbled themselves, and the wrath did not come in his days (2 Chronicles 32:26). The delay was mercy within the sentence. The lesson reached beyond whether the king could survive an immediate danger: the blessings entrusted to him required humility after the danger had passed, and the future of his house could not be measured only by peace during his own remaining years.

verses.text: At that time Berodach–baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present unto Hezekiah: for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

And Hezekiah hearkened unto them, and shewed them all the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the precious ointment, and all the house of his armour, and all that was found in his treasures: there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah shewed them not.
Then came Isaiah the prophet unto king Hezekiah, and said unto him, What said these men? and from whence came they unto thee? And Hezekiah said, They are come from a far country, even from Babylon.
And he said, What have they seen in thine house? And Hezekiah answered, All the things that are in mine house have they seen: there is nothing among my treasures that I have not shewed them.
And Isaiah said unto Hezekiah, Hear the word of the Lord.
Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store unto this day, shall be carried into Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the Lord.
And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
Then said Hezekiah unto Isaiah, Good is the word of the Lord which thou hast spoken. And he said, Is it not good, if peace and truth be in my days?
In those days Hezekiah was sick to the death, and prayed unto the Lord: and he spake unto him, and he gave him a sign.
But Hezekiah rendered not again according to the benefit done unto him; for his heart was lifted up: therefore there was wrath upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
Notwithstanding Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord came not upon them in the days of Hezekiah.

Howbeit in the business of the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who sent unto him to enquire of the wonder that was done in the land, God left him, to try him, that he might know all that was in his heart.
At that time Merodach–baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah: for he had heard that he had been sick, and was recovered.

And Hezekiah was glad of them, and shewed them the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the precious ointment, and all the house of his armour, and all that was found in his treasures: there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah shewed them not.

Then came Isaiah the prophet unto king Hezekiah, and said unto him, What said these men? and from whence came they unto thee? And Hezekiah said, They are come from a far country unto me, even from Babylon.
Then said he, What have they seen in thine house? And Hezekiah answered, All that is in mine house have they seen: there is nothing among my treasures that I have not shewed them.
Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, Hear the word of the Lord of hosts:
Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the Lord.
And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
Then said Hezekiah to Isaiah, Good is the word of the Lord which thou hast spoken. He said moreover, For there shall be peace and truth in my days.
In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon unto Jerusalem, and besieged it.

And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with part of the vessels of the house of God: which he carried into the land of Shinar to the house of his god; and he brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
And the king spake unto Ashpenaz the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring certain of the children of Israel, and of the king’s seed, and of the princes;

Children in whom was no blemish, but well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science, and such as had ability in them to stand in the king’s palace, and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans.

entries.commentary: Hezekiah falls sick unto death, and Isaiah brings the word to set his house in order, for he shall die and not live. Hezekiah turns his face to the wall and prays, asking the Most High to remember how he walked before Him in truth and with a perfect heart, and he weeps sore. Before Isaiah leaves the middle court the word returns: the Most High has heard his prayer and seen his tears, will heal him, add fifteen years, and defend the city for His own sake and for David's sake. Isaiah applies a lump of figs to the boil and Hezekiah recovers, showing that remedies and herbs go together with prayer, for healing is in the hand of the Most High. -

Hezekiah asks for a sign that the Most High will heal him and that he shall go up to the house of the Most High on the third day. Isaiah offers the shadow going forward ten degrees or back ten degrees, and Hezekiah answers that going forward is a light thing, but let it return backward ten degrees. Isaiah cries to the Most High and He brings the shadow ten degrees backward on the dial of Ahaz, reversing the natural course of the sun as proof of His power.

Berodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sends letters and a present to Hezekiah, having heard he had been sick; this is the introduction of Babylon, still only a province under Assyria at this time. Hezekiah hearkens to them and shows them all his precious things, his silver, gold, spices, ointment, and armor, holding nothing back, trusting his enemies because of the gift. Isaiah asks what the men saw and where they came from, then declares that all in the house shall be carried into Babylon, and Hezekiah's own sons shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. Hezekiah answers that the word of the Most High is good, content that peace and truth be in his days. This same account is given in [Isaiah 39](/bible/isaiah/39). -

The rest of the acts of Hezekiah, including how he made a pool and a conduit and brought water into the city, are written in the chronicles of the kings of Judah. Bringing water into the city is vision and planning like no other; this is nation building. Hezekiah sleeps with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigns in his stead.

After these acts of faithfulness Sennacherib king of Assyria enters Judah and encamps against the fenced cities, thinking to win them for himself. Hezekiah takes counsel to stop the waters of the fountains outside the city, repairs the broken wall, raises towers, builds another wall, and makes darts and shields in abundance. Our people are resourceful and skilled, doing the work themselves. He sets captains over the people and comforts them: be strong and courageous, for there be more with us than with him; with him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God to help us and fight our battles. -

Sennacherib sends servants to Jerusalem asking on what the people trust that they abide in the siege, and claims Hezekiah is persuading them to die by famine and thirst. He mocks that Hezekiah took away the high places and altars and commanded worship at one altar, twisting obedience to the commandment into a weakness. He argues that no god of any nation delivered its people from his hand, so neither will the God of Hezekiah. This is the same seed the world plants to make Israel weary and turn a people off one accord. -

Sennacherib's servants speak yet more against the Lord God and against his servant Hezekiah, and he writes letters to rail on the Lord God of Israel. They cry with a loud voice in the Jews' speech to the people on the wall to frighten and trouble them so they might take the city. They speak against the God of Jerusalem as against the gods of the peoples of the earth, which were only the work of men's hands. The one true God is the God of Israel, not an idol like the false gods of the nations.

Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amos, pray and cry to heaven over this railing. The Lord sends an angel that cuts off all the mighty men of valour, leaders, and captains in the camp of Assyria, so Sennacherib returns with shame to his own land, and his own sons slay him with the sword in the house of his god. Thus the Lord saves Hezekiah and Jerusalem and guides them on every side, and many bring gifts to the Lord and presents to Hezekiah, so he is magnified in the sight of all nations, a picture of the gifts the nations will bring back to Israel in the kingdom.

In those days Hezekiah is sick to death, prays to the Lord, and is given a sign. But Hezekiah renders not according to the benefit done to him, for his heart is lifted up in pride, and wrath comes upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem. When things go well, do not get puffed up and make it about yourself. Then Hezekiah humbles himself for the pride of his heart, he and the people of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord does not come upon them in his days. -

Hezekiah has exceeding riches and honour, making treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, and spices, and storehouses for corn, wine, oil, and cattle, for God gives him very much substance. He stops the upper watercourse of Gihon and brings it straight down to the west side of the city of David, and prospers in all his works, the plumbing he built for Jerusalem. When the ambassadors of Babylon come to inquire of the wonder, God leaves him to try him and know his heart. Hezekiah then sleeps with his fathers, is buried in honour among the sons of David, and Manasseh his son reigns in his stead. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Merodach-baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah, having heard he had been sick and recovered. Hezekiah was glad of them and showed them all the house of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the spices, the ointment, and all his armor, holding nothing back in all his dominion. Isaiah came and asked what the men had said and where they came from. When Hezekiah answered that they came from Babylon and had seen everything among his treasures, Isaiah declared the days would come when all in his house, and what his fathers had stored up, would be carried to Babylon with nothing left. The prophecy adds that Hezekiah's own sons that issue from him would be taken and made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. Hezekiah called the word of the Lord good because there would be peace and truth in his days. -

In the third year of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it, and the Most High gave Jehoiakim into his hand with part of the vessels of the house of God. Nebuchadnezzar carried those vessels into the land of Shinar to the house of his god and put them in his treasure house. This came to pass exactly as the prophets had warned. -

The king commanded to bring certain of the children of Israel, of the king's seed and of the princes: young men without blemish, well favoured, skilful in all wisdom, cunning in knowledge, understanding science, and able to stand in the king's palace. They took the best and the most educated among us, taught them the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans, and set them to build up their kingdom. It is the same thing today, where our people serve in the governments and the congresses and are used to build up a system that is not our own. Often those who are chosen are not loyal to their own people; they are assimilated to believe they are a part of the system and accepted by that society, and they are well rewarded for it. When our people were carried over in the dark ages they were a civilized, educated people, engineers and men of every profession, and they were used to serve and build up Babylon. Israel is the greatest nation the earth has known, and Babylon benefited off our wisdom and our knowledge. The king also appointed them a daily provision of the king's meat and of the wine which he drank.

Among those taken were of the children of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. The prince of the eunuchs gave them new names, Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, part of assimilating them into the king's service.
